```{=html}
<div class="home-ambient-stroke" aria-hidden="true">
  <svg viewBox="0 0 1000 100" preserveAspectRatio="none">
    <path id="home-ambient-fill" class="ambient-fill" d=""></path>
    <path id="home-ambient-path" class="ambient-line" d="" vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"></path>
  </svg>
</div>

<script>
(function () {
  const box = document.querySelector('.home-ambient-stroke');
  const line = document.getElementById('home-ambient-path');
  const fill = document.getElementById('home-ambient-fill');
  if (!box || !line || !fill) return;

  const W = 1000;            // viewBox width
  const H = 100;             // viewBox height
  const AMPLITUDE = H - 2;   // leave room for the stroke at the tallest peak
  const BINS = 240;          // grid of BINS + 1 points; also what counts as a
                             // distinct x-coordinate for the pointer
  const MAX_PAGE_FRACTION = 0.02;  // the curve never exceeds 2% of the page height
  const PRIOR_HEIGHT = 0.25 * AMPLITUDE;  // where the flat prior sits before any evidence
  const KERNEL_SIGMA = 0.05; // width of the bump added per unit, in normalised x
  const UNIT = 0.002;        // mass one unit of evidence carries, as a fraction
                             // of the whole distribution — also sets how long
                             // the curve remembers (half-life ~6s of ticks)
  const MIN_ENTROPY = 0.945; // floor on H(p), as a fraction of log(BINS + 1)
  const EASE = 0.14;         // how quickly the drawn curve catches up to the posterior
  const SETTLED = 1e-4 / (BINS + 1);  // residual below which the easing stops

  const N = BINS + 1;
  const UNIFORM = 1 / N;
  const ENTROPY_FLOOR = MIN_ENTROPY * Math.log(N);
  const clamp01 = (v) => (v < 0 ? 0 : v > 1 ? 1 : v);

  // The prior is flat: every x is equally likely until the reader gives us
  // evidence. `posterior` is a proper distribution — it always sums to one —
  // and `drawn` trails it so the curve grows smoothly rather than stepping.
  const posterior = new Float64Array(N).fill(UNIFORM);
  const drawn = Float64Array.from(posterior);

  let pointerX = 0.5;        // normalised; centre until the pointer says otherwise
  let lastBin = null;        // last x-coordinate the pointer occupied
  let lastScrollY = window.scrollY;
  let frame = 0;

  // Pre-computed kernel, indexed by bin offset, and scaled so that depositing
  // it adds exactly UNIT of mass — reflection at the ends conserves that mass.
  const KERNEL_REACH = Math.ceil(3.5 * KERNEL_SIGMA * BINS);
  const KERNEL = new Float64Array(KERNEL_REACH + 1);
  let kernelMass = 0;
  for (let o = -KERNEL_REACH; o <= KERNEL_REACH; o += 1) {
    const z = (o / BINS) / KERNEL_SIGMA;
    kernelMass += Math.exp(-0.5 * z * z);
  }
  for (let i = 0; i <= KERNEL_REACH; i += 1) {
    const z = (i / BINS) / KERNEL_SIGMA;
    KERNEL[i] = UNIT * Math.exp(-0.5 * z * z) / kernelMass;
  }

  // Deposit one unit of evidence at an x-coordinate. The kernel reflects off
  // the two ends so a bump at the edge of the page is not clipped to half its
  // height. Deposits are batched; `commit` turns them back into a distribution.
  function deposit(centre) {
    for (let o = -KERNEL_REACH; o <= KERNEL_REACH; o += 1) {
      const amount = KERNEL[o < 0 ? -o : o];
      let i = centre + o;
      if (i < 0) i = -i;                       // reflect at x = 0
      if (i > BINS) i = 2 * BINS - i;          // reflect at x = 1
      if (i >= 0 && i <= BINS) posterior[i] += amount;
    }
  }

  function entropyOfMix(lambda) {
    let h = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < N; i += 1) {
      const p = (1 - lambda) * posterior[i] + lambda * UNIFORM;
      if (p > 0) h -= p * Math.log(p);
    }
    return h;
  }

  // Rescale to unit mass, then hold the distribution above a minimum entropy by
  // mixing it back towards uniform. Without this the pointer sitting still —
  // which now deposits on every tick — would grind the curve into a spike.
  function settle() {
    let mass = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < N; i += 1) mass += posterior[i];
    for (let i = 0; i < N; i += 1) posterior[i] /= mass;

    if (entropyOfMix(0) >= ENTROPY_FLOOR) return;

    let lo = 0;                // too concentrated
    let hi = 1;                // uniform, so certainly above the floor
    for (let step = 0; step < 14; step += 1) {
      const mid = (lo + hi) / 2;
      if (entropyOfMix(mid) < ENTROPY_FLOOR) lo = mid; else hi = mid;
    }
    for (let i = 0; i < N; i += 1) {
      posterior[i] = (1 - hi) * posterior[i] + hi * UNIFORM;
    }
  }

  function commit() {
    settle();
    animate();
  }

  // The band is sized in pixels so the tallest peak sits exactly at the cap;
  // the viewBox then maps the density onto it.
  function resize() {
    const cap = document.documentElement.scrollHeight * MAX_PAGE_FRACTION;
    box.style.height = cap.toFixed(2) + 'px';
  }

  function render() {
    // Scale by total mass, so the curve reads as a distribution: concentrating
    // probability in one place lowers it everywhere else. Once the peak would
    // breach the cap, the whole curve is scaled down to stay inside it.
    let mass = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i <= BINS; i += 1) mass += drawn[i];
    let scale = mass > 0 ? (PRIOR_HEIGHT * (BINS + 1)) / mass : 0;

    let peak = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i <= BINS; i += 1) {
      if (drawn[i] > peak) peak = drawn[i];
    }
    if (peak * scale > AMPLITUDE) scale = AMPLITUDE / peak;

    let d = '';
    for (let i = 0; i <= BINS; i += 1) {
      const x = (W / BINS) * i;
      const y = H - drawn[i] * scale;
      d += (i === 0 ? 'M ' : ' L ') + x.toFixed(2) + ' ' + y.toFixed(2);
    }

    line.setAttribute('d', d);
    fill.setAttribute('d', d + ' L ' + W + ' ' + H + ' L 0 ' + H + ' Z');
  }

  // Every tick counts: as long as we know where the pointer is, each one banks
  // a unit of evidence there, whether or not anything is moving. The loop keeps
  // running while the pointer is on the page, and afterwards just long enough
  // for the drawn curve to catch up.
  function tick() {
    if (lastBin !== null) {
      deposit(lastBin);
      settle();
    }

    let moved = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i <= BINS; i += 1) {
      const delta = posterior[i] - drawn[i];
      drawn[i] += delta * EASE;
      const size = delta < 0 ? -delta : delta;
      if (size > moved) moved = size;
    }

    render();

    if (lastBin !== null || moved > SETTLED) {
      frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tick);
    } else {
      for (let i = 0; i <= BINS; i += 1) drawn[i] = posterior[i];
      frame = 0;
      render();
    }
  }

  function animate() {
    if (!frame) frame = window.requestAnimationFrame(tick);
  }

  // Moving the pointer is itself evidence: one unit for every x-coordinate it
  // enters. Standing still adds nothing more (the single unit was banked on
  // arrival), and moving straight up or down adds nothing at all.
  window.addEventListener('pointermove', function (event) {
    pointerX = clamp01(event.clientX / window.innerWidth);
    const bin = Math.round(pointerX * BINS);
    if (bin === lastBin) return;

    if (lastBin === null) {
      deposit(bin);                       // first sighting: a single unit
    } else {
      const step = bin > lastBin ? 1 : -1;
      for (let b = lastBin + step; b !== bin + step; b += step) deposit(b);
    }

    lastBin = bin;
    commit();
  }, { passive: true });

  // A pointer that has left the page is no longer evidence for anything, and
  // coordinates crossed off-screen were never entered — so it comes back as a
  // first sighting rather than sweeping across everything in between.
  document.addEventListener('pointerleave', function () {
    lastBin = null;
  });

  // Every tick in which the page is scrolling — in either direction — adds
  // one unit wherever the pointer happens to be.
  window.addEventListener('scroll', function () {
    if (window.scrollY === lastScrollY) return;
    lastScrollY = window.scrollY;
    deposit(Math.round(pointerX * BINS));
    commit();
  }, { passive: true });

  window.addEventListener('resize', resize);
  window.addEventListener('load', resize);

  resize();
  render();
})();
</script>
```

<!-- <p class="home-intro-quote">How does an agent's model of other agents shape what the collective becomes? And how do we measure and govern that?</p> -->

<!-- I am interested in how agency compounds. Groups can do things that their individual members cannot, but collective capability brings coordination costs and difficult questions about who performs which role, who receives the resulting benefits, how power and resources are distributed, and how tragedies of the commons arise. I regard these as exceptionally important problems: solving them well would amount to resolving many of the obstacles to highly beneficial collective organization.

My background includes robotics, control theory, reinforcement learning, game theory, information theory, and active inference. I am especially interested in understanding multi-agent systems through information-theoretic and game-theoretic lenses and in determining how individual agents can compose into something resembling a higher-level or “super” agent. -->

I am fascinated by the capacity of collectives to achieve outcomes beyond the reach of isolated individuals. My research investigates the interplay between individual agency and collective dynamics, focusing on how incentives shape this relationship. I draw upon models from cognitive science and computational economics, analysing them through a complex systems framework that incorporates information theory, dynamical systems theory, game theory, and Bayesian inference.

Passionate about empowering individuals equitably and sustainably, I believe that democratizing information and technology, along with fostering local communities, will have the greatest impact toward this goal.

I have studies in robotics and mechatronics engineering, statistics and data science, complex systems, AI. I have experience in deep reinforcement learning and computer vision research. I'm a certified AWS Solutions Architect Associate with several years of industry experience in cloud infrastructure and 10 years of Python expertise in automation, data engineering, and machine learning.
